chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman whom a man married, and he found that she already had a husband. He (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is the whipping, and upon her is the stoning, because he proceeded without knowledge, and she proceeded with knowledge. And his expiation, if one does not proceed to the Imam, is that he should give in charity five Aswaa' of fine flour.

key_terms.أَصْوُعِ دَقِيقٍ: Five Aswaa' of fine flour (a unit of volume)

ai.seo_question: What are the hadd penalties for a woman and man in a case of polyandry or remarriage during the waiting period according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes the hadd penalties based on the woman's prior knowledge of her marital status, assigning the more severe punishment of rajm (stoning) to her and jald (whipping) to the man who married in ignorance. It further clarifies the procedural aspect of expiation (kaffarah), specifying a donation of five sa' of flour if the ruling is not immediately executed by the Imam, reflecting the practical application of fiqh in judicial contexts.
